paras.text: i. The prefix n– (from normal) is used for those alkanes in which all the carbon atoms are in one continuous straight chain.

paras.text: ii. The prefix iso– is used for those alkanes which have a methyl group (CH₃–) attached to the second last carbon atom of the continuous chain.

paras.text: iii. The prefix neo– is used for those alkanes which have two methyl groups attached to the second last carbon atom of the continuous chain.

In the tert–butyl group, it is tertiary (3°) or bonded to three other carbon atoms.

sections.theory:
i. The prefix n– (from normal) is used for those alkanes in which all the carbon atoms are in one continuous straight chain.

ii. The prefix iso– is used for those alkanes which have a methyl group (CH₃–) attached to the second last carbon atom of the continuous chain.

iii. The prefix neo– is used for those alkanes which have two methyl groups attached to the second last carbon atom of the continuous chain.

Alkyl group (R–)

Alkyl group contain a hydrogen atom less than alkane and represented by R– having general formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₁. The name of alkyl group is derived by replacing the –ane suffix of the corresponding alkane with –yl. Methane becomes methyl (CH₃–); ethane becomes ethyl (CH₃CH₂–) and so on. The dash at the end of the chain represents a potential point of attachment for some other atom or group of atoms. Some of the alkyl groups are shown below.

The names of the secondary–butyl (sec–butyl) and tertiary–butyl (tert–butyl or t–butyl) groups are based on the degree of alkyl substitution of the carbon atom attached to the main chain. In the sec–butyl group, the carbon atom bonded to the main chain is secondary (2°) or bonded to two other carbon atoms. In the tert–butyl group, it is tertiary (3°) or bonded to three other carbon atoms.

(b) IUPAC System

In this system the parent names of the alkanes are retained such as methane, ethane, propane, butane, pentane, hexane and so on while the branching (if any) is treated as substituent, attached to the main continuous carbon chain.

Rules for naming of alkanes:

1. Find the longest continuous chain of carbon atoms and use this chain as the base name or parent or stem name.

2. Number the longest chain, beginning with the end nearest a branch.

اس نظام میں الکینز کے اصل نام برقرار رہتے ہیں، مثلاً میتھین، ایتھین، پروپین، بیوٹین، پینٹین، ہیکسین اور اسی طرح آگے؛ جبکہ شاخ (اگر موجود ہو) کو مرکزی مسلسل کاربن زنجیر سے جڑا متبادل سمجھا جاتا ہے۔

الکینز کی نام گذاری کے قواعد:

1. کاربن ایٹموں کی سب سے لمبی مسلسل زنجیر تلاش کریں اور اس زنجیر کو بنیادی نام یا اصل نام یا جڑ کے نام کے طور پر استعمال کریں۔

2. سب سے لمبی زنجیر کو اس سرے سے نمبر دیں جو کسی شاخ کے سب سے قریب ہو۔

په الکایل ګروپ کې د الکان په پرتله یو هایدروجن اټوم کم وي او په R– ښودل کېږي؛ عمومي فورمول یې CₙH₂ₙ₊₁ دی. د الکایل ګروپ نوم د اړوند الکان د –ane وروستاړي پر ځای د –yl په ایښودلو جوړېږي. میتان په میتایل (CH₃–)، ایتان په ایتایل (CH₃CH₂–) بدلېږي او همداسې نور. د ځنځیر په پای کې کرښه د بل اټوم یا د اټومونو د ګروپ د نښلېدو احتمالي ځای ښيي. ځینې الکایل ګروپونه لاندې ښودل شوي دي.

i. The prefix n– (from normal) is used for those alkanes in which all the carbon atoms are in one continuous straight chain.

ii. The prefix iso– is used for those alkanes which have a methyl group (CH₃–) attached to the second last carbon atom of the continuous chain.

iii. The prefix neo– is used for those alkanes which have two methyl groups attached to the second last carbon atom of the continuous chain.

Alkyl group (R–)

Alkyl group contain a hydrogen atom less than alkane and represented by R– having general formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₁. The name of alkyl group is derived by replacing the –ane suffix of the corresponding alkane with –yl. Methane becomes methyl (CH₃–); ethane becomes ethyl (CH₃CH₂–) and so on. The dash at the end of the chain represents a potential point of attachment for some other atom or group of atoms. Some of the alkyl groups are shown below.

The names of the secondary–butyl (sec–butyl) and tertiary–butyl (tert–butyl or t–butyl) groups are based on the degree of alkyl substitution of the carbon atom attached to the main chain. In the sec–butyl group, the carbon atom bonded to the main chain is secondary (2°) or bonded to two other carbon atoms. In the tert–butyl group, it is tertiary (3°) or bonded to three other carbon atoms.

(b) IUPAC System

In this system the parent names of the alkanes are retained such as methane, ethane, propane, butane, pentane, hexane and so on while the branching (if any) is treated as substituent, attached to the main continuous carbon chain.

Rules for naming of alkanes:

1. Find the longest continuous chain of carbon atoms and use this chain as the base name or parent or stem name.

2. Number the longest chain, beginning with the end nearest a branch.
